title: Two neighbors
text: Two power companies share a river, but plan their work without seeing each other. The Savannah River is the border: Georgia Power builds on the Georgia side, Dominion Energy on the South Carolina side.

title: Their plans
text: Dominion plans 54 jobs. Georgia Power plans 60. Nobody lines them up. MrGridy put every one of them on one map, from their public filings.

title: Where they collide
text: Of 2,580 possible pairs, only 50 are within a crew's morning drive, forty kilometers. Two of them touch outright.

title: The best match
text: These two jobs touch. One crew, one yard, one permit instead of two. Dominion's Okatie to McIntosh 115 kilovolt Tie, and Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh expansion. Both are under construction at the same time for about 7 months.

title: What it saves
text: What working together could save: roughly $2.1 million across all 50 matches, somewhere between $1 million and $3.1 million. It is an estimate. Georgia Power does not publish its project costs, so real savings could be higher.

title: When a storm comes
text: About 51 hours before Hurricane Helene arrived, MrGridy predicted where lines would break for both companies, and compared it with what happened. It simulated the storm 500 times, with physics.

title: Fix it together
text: Working together, power comes back about 9.7 hours sooner, and 3.2 hours sooner for people who rely on powered medical equipment. Shared staging yards and crews go to the nearest repair zone first, whichever company owns it. Two neighbors, one plan.

title: Corridor fly-through
text: This is the number one match, near Rincon, Georgia. In teal, DESC's Okatie to McIntosh 115 kilovolt Tie. In orange, Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh expansion. Here the two projects touch, so their outages have to be planned together. They could share outage coordination, right-of-way, access roads and permits. One staging yard, right beside both jobs, would serve both crews. And for about 7 months, both crews are due to be here at the same time.

title: Storm crew briefing: Helene
text: Storm crew briefing for Hurricane Helene. On the Georgia side, the heaviest outages are expected in Chatham County, Richmond County and Columbia County, with about 772,000 customers out across Georgia at the peak. On the South Carolina side, watch Beaufort County, York County and Aiken County, with about 384,000 customers out statewide. The simulation expects roughly 400 damaged transmission sections on Georgia Power's system and one on DESC's. Both utilities stage jointly at Augusta, Georgia, which reaches two repair zones within 56 minutes. Vulnerable areas first. Start near Pierce County, where about 1,700 residents rely on powered medical equipment, then Lowndes County and Jeff Davis County. Working together, power comes back about 9.7 hours sooner. Zone order is live on the MrGridy map. Stay safe.

title: Storm crew briefing: Helene (español)
text: Informes para las cuadrillas de tormenta sobre el huracán Helene. Del lado de Georgia, se esperan los mayores apagones en Chatham County, Richmond County y Columbia County, con unos 772,000 clientes sin servicio en todo Georgia en el punto máximo. Del lado de Carolina del Sur, vigilen Beaufort County, York County y Aiken County, con unos 384,000 clientes sin servicio a nivel estatal. La simulación espera aproximadamente 400 secciones de transmisión dañadas en el sistema de Georgia Power y una en el de DESC. Ambas empresas de servicios públicos se concentran conjuntamente en Augusta, Georgia, lo que permite llegar a dos zonas de reparación en un plazo de 56 minutos. Las áreas vulnerables primero. Comiencen cerca de Pierce County, donde unos 1,700 residentes dependen de equipos médicos conectados a la corriente, luego Lowndes County y Jeff Davis County. Trabajando juntos, la energía se restablece unas 9.7 horas antes. El orden de las zonas está disponible en tiempo real en el mapa de MrGridy. Cuídense.

title: Spark
text: a single subtle electric spark crackle, short and clean, close up, no music

title: Grid hum
text: a soft low electrical substation hum, steady and calm, seamless loop, no music
